Here's a crash course on the evolution of money.

Level 0 -- Barter system: Here you have trade but no money. Bartering sucks because merchants don't want to trade for goods that are bulky or perishable or that they don't understand the value of or that are hard to get rid of.

Level 1 -- Specie: Certain commodities have near universal acceptance by merchants. Good forms of specie are dense in value, of uniform quality, and able to be stored indefinitely until consumed. Small pieces of rare metals are ideal for this, but other forms of specie currency have become common in certain markets. A government or non-government entity might facilitate trade by stamping some of these metal pieces as having an indicated weight and purity. Skeptical merchants can still weigh and examine coins themselves, so no one has to trust the mint very much.

Level 2 -- Banking: Some families began offering banking services to hold their customers gold and silver coins in their secure vaults for a fee. The bankers probably intended that someone would withdraw their coins from the bank to bring into town and buy a horse. The horse trader would then likely return to the bank to deposit the coins and the bank would collect the Middle Age equivalent of an ATM fee on both transactions.

Level 3 -- Fiat Money: But often as not, what actually happened was that the buyer would simply exchange the banknotes representing a deposit directly with the seller without first cashing them in for specie money. This was bad for the bank since they lost out on transaction fees when their banknotes were themselves used as currency. But it was also really, really good for the bank once they realized that this meant they could issue banknotes for money they didn't have. For the first time in history, people could create money without creating wealth. Banking had evolved from a money storage service to moneylenders and money issuers. This also now meant that a bank with irresponsible practices could crash an economy if their notes were suddenly recognized as worthless.
